moduleEvidence.title: Korean 1
entry:
This course is meant for BA students in Korean Studies. Limited elective spaces exist for other students. There are no admission requirements.

**Prerequisite**: Students should know how to read and write Korean alphabet, Hangeul, prior to joining the course. The online lessons in the following [link ](https://rise.articulate.com/share/m33YjGuAFH2YAPhd7qklG55JajU02YAv#/)may help.

moduleEvidence.title: Korean language in use
entry:
This course is intended for BA students in Korean Studies who have successfully completed either Korean 3 (5722KK03) or Korean Language Study in Korea (5722VK07, TOPIK level 3 or equivalent).

Limited elective spaces are available for students from other programs. If you are not a Korean Studies major, please contact Dr. A.R. Nam to confirm whether your Korean language proficiency is sufficient to enroll in this course.

moduleEvidence.title: Intermediate Korean Reading 1
entry:
This course is intended for BA students in Korean Studies who have successfully completed either Korean 3 (5722KK03) or Korean Language Study in Korea (5722VK07, level 3 or equivalent).

Limited elective spaces are available for students from other programs. If you are not a Korean Studies major, please contact Dr. A.R. Nam to confirm whether your Korean language proficiency is sufficient to enroll in this course.

**Please note**: this course replaces Hanja and Vocabulary (5722VKH) and KAP: Hanja and Advanced Vocabulary (5722VKH1). Students that started the BA Koreastudies in 2022-2023 or earlier and did not finish any of these courses, can make use of a transitional arrangement as listed in the remarks below.

moduleEvidence.title: BA eindwerkstuk seminar
entry:
This course is only available for Korean studies students who have successfully completed one of the BA3 content seminars.

Before the start of the seminar, students are expected to submit a thesis proposal including a research question and 300-word problem statement to their assigned supervisor for the BA thesis (who may be different than the seminar instructor). This submission is through Brightspace.

moduleEvidence.title: Business Korean
entry:
This course is intended for BA students in Korean Studies who have successfully completed all BA2 Korean language courses. 

Limited elective spaces are available for students from other programs. If you are not a Korean Studies major, please contact Dr. A.R. Nam (a.r.nam@hum.leidenuniv.nl) to confirm whether your Korean language proficiency is sufficient to enroll in this course.

moduleEvidence.title: Topical Reading: Contemporary Korea and Digital Humanities
entry: This course is only available for BA3 students in Korean Studies who have successfully completed all BA1 and BA2 courses.

moduleEvidence.title: BA Final paper
entry:
Only Korean studies students who have successfully completed all courses in BA1, BA2, and the first semester of BA3 and are enrolled in or have successfully completed the Thesis Seminar may write a BA Final Paper (thesis).

Students can apply for supervision submitted by via the *[BA Korean Studies Registration for Thesis Supervision form](https://fd24.formdesk.com/universiteitleiden/KSBA3TS)* until **February 1, 2027**.

annualGroups: Year one 50 EC required plus two 5 EC choices. Year two 20 EC required plus restricted blocks of 10, 10, 15 and 5 EC. Year three seminar 5 EC, restricted 5 and 10 EC, final paper 10 EC and two open 15 EC blocks. Semester allocations are 30 EC each. Themes and Approaches uses the 10 EC group and module metadata. Noncredit mentorship is separate. Korean 3 uses the Leiden alternative. The annual catalogue and individual module records establish the current choices and entry conditions despite the regulations URL returning access HTML. The dated official guide corroborates the structure but does not control current module details.
progression: Annual BA-KOR programme groups and module records establish the 180 EC Leiden-based Korean 3 example. The year-two Themes and Approaches group and module both carry 10 EC. Year three has 15 EC of specialist choices, a 5 EC thesis seminar, a 10 EC final paper and 30 EC of genuinely open study. Mentorship carries zero credit. Korean 1 requires prior Hangeul literacy, Korean 2 follows Korean 1 and Korean 3 follows Korean 2. Korean language in use and both selected intermediate reading courses follow Korean 3. Topical Reading requires completion of years one and two. Business Korean follows all year-two language courses. The topical seminar is completed in semester one before the thesis seminar. The final paper requires completion of years one and two and first-semester year-three courses, plus enrollment in or completion of the thesis seminar.
interestAccounting: Nine generating interests (13520–13528), 13 curricular supporting topics and ten search illustrations or career/further-study contexts. Literature is genuinely available in the annual restricted curriculum. Digital Korea and Topical Reading substantiate study of digital and cultural phenomena without treating individual media genres or occupations as standalone study directions. The 2026–2027 Divided Korea and Topical Reading records substantiate peninsula division, social science and North–South analysis. Hangul, language registers and literary traditions support the main language and cultural interest. No career guarantee is inferred.
